name: stage-warp-mesh
summary: a generic stage of mocha-stage: each frame warped by a triangle mesh with barycentric interpolation inside each triangle, with the mesh-warp crate for the coordinates and the resample crate for the samples; a published method under explicit configuration, not compared with any product

binaries.name: mocha-stage
binaries.arguments: apply warp-mesh --width W --height H --depth 8|16|32 --fps N[/D] [--frames N] [--describe] [--param K=V]... [--layer mesh=PATH]
binaries.stdin: whole raw frames; not read with --describe
binaries.stdout: the frames of the stage, nothing else; with --describe one line of JSON
binaries.stderr: empty on exit 0; exactly one line error: CODE: MESSAGE on a failure

frame_contract: frames/2 raw frames: depth 8 is packed rgba (4 bytes per pixel), depth 16 is packed rgba64le (8 bytes), depth 32 is planar gbrapf32le (16 bytes, planes G, B, R, A, 1.0 is full scale); whole frames back to back, no header, no padding, straight alpha, a frame of at most 4 GiB; a stream that ends inside a frame is a partial frame

parameters.maps_to: Output width in pixels; 0 keeps the input width.
Output height in pixels; 0 keeps the input height.

parameters.accepts: nearest, bilinear, keys, mitchell, lanczos, box
parameters.maps_to: The reconstruction filter (Config::filter).
The parameter a of the Keys cubic; read when filter is keys.
The parameter B of the Mitchell and Netravali cubic; read when filter is mitchell.
The parameter C of the Mitchell and Netravali cubic; read when filter is mitchell.
The lobes per side of the Lanczos filter; read when filter is lanczos.
What a tap outside the image reads (Config::border).
Whether pixel i has its centre at i + 0.5 or at i (Config::center).
Whether colour is interpolated as it is or multiplied by alpha first and divided afterwards (Config::alpha).
Whether the result is divided by the sum of the tap weights (Config::normalize).
Where the nearest filter goes when the coordinate is halfway between two pixels (Config::tie).
The order of the accumulation loop, which matters for rounding only (Config::order).
The size of the box filter in source pixels: one pixel, or the mapped output pixel (Config::footprint).
Which triangle owns a point on a shared edge or vertex: the containing triangle of lowest index, or the one the fill rule of Pineda 1988 names (Config::tie).
What a point in no triangle maps to: nothing, the nearest point of the mesh, or the extended map of the nearest triangle (Config::outside).
Whether triangles of both orientations are taken or all must turn the same way (Config::winding).
The formula of the barycentric coordinates, which matters for rounding only (Config::bary).
Whether triangles of no area are taken and skipped or refused (Config::allow_degenerate).
The size of the grid that speeds up point location: the square root of the triangle count per side, or grid_cols by grid_rows (Config::grid).
The columns of the location grid; read when grid is fixed.
The rows of the location grid; read when grid is fixed.

layers.meaning: A mesh file: vertices with a source and an output position in pixels, and triangles. Without it every position maps to itself.

geometry: declared: the output is width by height, where 0 keeps the input side; the frame count, the depth and the rate are those of the request; --describe answers the output geometry without reading standard input and without opening a layer; a keyed parameter never changes the geometry
sample_rule: computed on f32 samples: an integer sample v is v / 255 or v / 65535, computed in f64 and rounded once to f32; on the way out a sample x is floor(clamp(x, 0, 1) * max + 0.5) and a sample that is not a number is 0; depth 32 samples are the stream's own floats and are never clamped; each output pixel is sampled by the resample crate at the source position the map of the stage gives for it, under the filter, border, pixel centre, alpha and normalisation rule of the parameters; a pixel without a source position is zero in all four channels; the map is Warp::inverse of the mesh-warp crate: the output position located in the output positions of the mesh reads the source at the same barycentric coordinates; a position in no triangle follows outside; without the mesh layer every position maps to itself
mesh_form: the text form mesh-1: the first line that is not empty and not a comment is the word mesh-1; a line whose first word starts with # and an empty line are skipped; vertex SX SY DX DY adds a vertex with its position in the source frame and its position in the output frame, four finite decimal numbers, vertices numbered from 0 in the order of the file; triangle A B C adds a triangle of three vertex numbers; positions are in pixels, x to the right and y down, a frame of w by h pixels spans 0 to w and 0 to h and pixel i has its centre at i + 0.5; the file holds one mesh, used for every frame
error_line: error: CODE: MESSAGE, one line on standard error, where CODE is usage, unsupported, bad_input, partial_frame, broken_pipe or stage_failed

exit_codes_table.means: every input frame was processed and written, or --describe printed its answer
stage_failed: the output could not be written for a reason other than a closed pipe
usage: a bad or missing option, a parameter or a layer given twice, a layer with an empty path
unsupported: a depth the stage does not take, a parameter or a layer the stage does not have, a value the stage refuses, a transform or a layer content the configuration refuses
bad_input, partial_frame or broken_pipe: a failed read, input that ends inside a frame, a frame count other than --frames, a layer file that cannot be read or parsed, a reader that went away
exit_codes_table.table: the table's bad_input, partial_frame and broken_pipe

unpinned_paths.why: a write to standard output that fails for a reason other than a closed pipe; no test makes one, because it needs a device that differs between systems
a reader that closes the pipe while the stage writes; tests/stage_<id>.rs and the convention's conformance tool exercise it, the rows of this file do not
